crime: Every snowy dusk, one of the prisoners shaped a snow rabbit for each girl along the fountain in the courtyard, and she always set {WITCH_NAME}'s beside her own. The first time the girl took her hand, {WITCH_NAME} used her Magic to turn her skin stove-hot and burned her fingers. The girl came back in mittens, and from then on she held {WITCH_NAME}'s hand every dusk.
Then one dusk she let go to pull her mittens onto a prisoner who stood shivering. "You're always warm," she told {WITCH_NAME}. "You don't need them."

{WITCH_NAME}'s mother had come home only some nights, and on those nights she wrapped her daughter inside her coat. One winter night she unbuttoned the coat from around her and wrapped the new baby in it instead. "You're a big girl. Keep yourself warm."

Once the shivering prisoner had gone inside, {WITCH_NAME} pressed the girl's face into the snow on the fountain rim until she stopped moving. Then she gathered her into her lap and held her, skin stove-hot, until the girl's cheeks and hands were warm again. She laid her back in the snow, went to the dining hall, and sat down to supper among the other prisoners.

Before supper ended, the prisoners found the girl by the fountain, her cheek still warm, as if she had been alive only minutes before. In the trial court they ruled that she had been attacked after {WITCH_NAME} sat down to supper. Whoever did it, it was never the one at the table.

Then a prisoner lifted the dead girl's coat and found two handprints scorched into the back, brown singe in the wool. The court saw it then: stove-hot hands had held the warmth in, and she had died before supper began.
fields.epitaph: She kept a warmth at last, by holding someone who could no longer leave.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Keeps Herself Warm
execution: Two snow rabbits rose from the execution stand, frozen hard and as tall as the trial court, sitting flank to flank. She stood shut in the narrow hollow between their icy sides. The rabbits began to slide toward each other, and the hollow narrowed. She turned her skin stove-hot and pushed both palms against the ice. Steam poured up where her hands pressed. The flanks closed on her shoulders and chest, and kept closing. At last the two rabbits stood pressed flank to flank, and the steam thinned, and stopped rising.

magic.name: Kettle and Frost
magic.text: She can make her skin stove-hot or ice-cold at will, and never feels it herself.
